headline: Controlled experiments report answer-prior bias across eight dense retrievers
summary: A Nov 8 arXiv paper reports that, across eight dense retrievers, a model's preference for a canonical answer predicts higher retrieval scores for passages containing that answer. In controlled LAMA/TREx template contrasts, this relationship also appears when the answer-matching passage expresses the wrong relation. The authors report positive correlations in both settings; their selected examples are single-token cases where the diagnostic already favors the canonical object. The study does not measure prevalence in natural corpora or downstream RAG outcomes.
